title: Superconducting cavity probes sliding ferroelectricity in small-angle twisted WSe$_2$
authors: Krishnendu Maji, Supriya Mandal, Sriram H., Rishiraj Rajkhowa, Malhar Date, Sayani Pal, Meghan P. Patankar, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Vibhor Singh, Mandar M. Deshmukh
abstract: Ferroelectricity is a property of materials that exhibit spontaneous charge polarization. Ferroelectricity in 2D materials is interesting because of their applications in memory devices and field-effect transistors. Recently, a new type of ferroelectricity, known as sliding ferroelectricity, has been discovered, in which parallel-stacked bilayers of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) or transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) develop an out-of-plane electric polarization. In this work, we probe the polarization of small-angle parallel stacked WSe$_2$ by measuring its high-frequency AC response, achieved by embedding it into a half-wave superconducting coplanar waveguide cavity. We observe a hysteretic response in the capacitance of the stack and quality factor of the cavity, confirming ferroelectric switching in the system. Our results further reveal relaxation effects associated with ferroelectric domain-wall motion. This cavity-based technique has potential applications in probing domain-wall dynamics in a ferroelectric system at high frequencies.
summary: Researchers used a superconducting microwave cavity setup to measure the electrical response of small-angle twisted WSe2. They confirmed the presence of ferroelectricity by observing characteristic hysteresis loops in capacitance and quality factor. This technique provides a high-frequency tool for studying domain-wall dynamics in 2D ferroelectric materials.
main_problem: The study aims to probe the signature of sliding ferroelectricity within small-angle twisted WSe2 heterostructures.
main_result: Hysteretic responses in both capacitance and cavity quality factor were observed, confirming ferroelectric switching dynamics associated with domain-wall motion at high frequencies.
method: The polarization is probed by embedding the material into a superconducting coplanar waveguide (CPW) cavity and measuring its high-frequency AC response using microwave transmission spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The physical system is a small-angle parallel stacked WSe2 heterostructure, which exhibits ferroelectricity due to stacking-induced symmetry breaking. This structure acts as the coupling capacitor within an superconducting CPW cavity.
key_observables: Hysteretic response in capacitance and internal quality factor ($Q_i$); changes in resonant frequency ($	ilde{S}_{21}$ magnitude/phase).
important_parameters: Coercive field ($\sim 0.14 	ext{ V/nm}$ for $0.1^\circ$ twist); operating temperature (e.g., $1.5 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The measurement technique is sensitive to domain-wall dynamics at high frequencies, and the observed hysteresis originates specifically from the t-WSe2 layer, not the hBN layers.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic device setups (heterostructure coupled to cavity), measured $	ilde{S}_{21}$ data showing resonant features, and plots demonstrating capacitance and $Q_i$ hysteresis versus applied gate voltage.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical setup using superconducting cavities, measures the complex dielectric susceptibility via microwave spectroscopy, analyzes the resulting hysteresis in C and Q, and uses control experiments to confirm the ferroelectric origin of the signal.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter ferroelectrics, the use of high-frequency cavity measurements to probe domain dynamics is analogous to characterizing dissipation mechanisms in open quantum systems or superconducting qubits coupled to lossy environments.
